newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-STANDARD BANK CUP SET TO BE PLAYED LATER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STANDARD BANK CUP SET TO BE PLAYED LATER.

text.p: The virgin Standard Bank cricket cup is set to be given a new showpiece position at the end of the South African season.
Ali Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board, told Reuters on Tuesday he was recommending to his executive committee that the eight-team competition start two months later.
It is currently scheduled to take place between February 18 and March 13 but would clash with the first test match against Australia and several other high-profile matches, Bacher said.
He is proposing that it now start on April 14 -- the day after the final one-day international against Australia -- with the final taking place on May 2.
"It makes sense to the sponsors and myself," Bacher said. "We have also spoken to Supersport which has agreed to televise every ball that is bowled in the competition if it is moved."
"The whole nation will be focused on it. At the moment it is placed against the Australians, who are a big draw card, and there are other important games going on at the time."
The executive committee will consider the proposal in Johannesburg on Saturday and if they agree to it, it will mean the latest-ever finish to a South African season.
Standard Bank took over the sponsorship of the popular day-night series from Benson and Hedges this season, introducing the complementary cup competition.
The 11-team Standard Bank League is contested on a straight league basis and concludes on December 21. The top six teams then join Kenya and Mashonaland to contest the cup.
